newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends lower with soft cash, charts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends lower with soft cash, charts.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, pressured by a soft physical market, ended lower Tuesday in sluggish activity, and traders said June's close below support today may signal more downside.
Spot-June slipped 3.5 cents to close at $2.189 per million British thermal units. July settled 2.2 cents lower at $2.209. Other deferreds ended down by two to three cents.

"There's no weather for the next two weeks and the technicals look terrible. I think we'll see more long liquidation tomorrow," said one Midwest trader, adding a soft physical market also would help pressure the board lower.
With little extreme weather this week to stir heating or cooling loads, most expected cash to hold or move lower near-term despite steady injection demand.
But they said the likely arrival soon of better air conditioning demand should temper the bears.

Forecasters expected only limited cooling demand this week in Texas and the South, with normal to below-normal East and Midwest temperatures offering a slim chance for modest heating loads. Hot weather will persist in the Southwest.
Estimates for a build in Wednesday's weekly AGA storage report still ranged from 50 to 80 bcf.

Chart traders, citing still-sizeable open interest, said June's close today below $2.19 could trigger more long liquidation near-term, with a move to major support in the $2.05 area a possibility. Minor support was seen at $2.14-15. Resistance was now pegged at $2.28-29 and then at the contract high of $2.43.
Maintenance work on Transco's Texas line, which began Saturday, will cut the line's total capacity of about 600 mmcfd from May 14-19, with 400 mmcfd still cut for May 20-22.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped more than a nickel Tuesday to the high-teens. Midcon pipes were down a similar amount to the high-$1.90s. New York city gate gas skidded a dime or more to the low-$2.40s.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip fell 2.6 cents to $2.233. NYMEX said 30,555 contracts traded, down slightly from Monday's revised tally of 31,694.

On the KCBT, June finished 5.4 cents lower at $2.026, while deferreds ended down by 2.5 to 3.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.9 cents to 1.9 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 335 contracts traded, up from Monday's total of 193.
